subject: Catalyst: packaging options, price-match request
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen@catalyst.ai>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@catalyst.ai, Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@catalyst.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing and packaging clarification (RFP attached)

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Catalyst leadership liked the latency profile and the console telemetry. Procurement asked me to send the RFP and the competitor offer we discussed. Attached: Catalyst_RFP_Q3.pdf.

Short version of their ask: our incumbent has offered a 25% effective discount on list pricing plus a $150k onboarding credit if we sign a 24-month committed term. They also guarantee certain seat-tier pricing and a ramp schedule tied to monthly committed units.

Can Redwood match on economics or provide an equivalent packaging that keeps total TCO neutral for Catalyst? Two critical items for them:
- A clear seat/seat-tier mapping (we have 3 seat types: dev, prod, enterprise)
- An onboarding credit or staged credit to offset migration egress and integration hours

We'd prefer a simple, repackaged offer rather than a long negotiation. Would you be able to outline matching options and any constraints (SLA uplift, support tier, term minimums)?

Thanks,
Ellen
Ellen Park
Head of Platform Partnerships
Catalyst AI

Attachments: Catalyst_RFP_Q3.pdf (application/pdf, 1.2MB)

From: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@catalyst.ai>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing and packaging clarification (RFP attached)

Ellen — appreciate the quick context and the RFP. I looped in Jonas (solutions) and Marissa (commercial) so we can cover both the runtime/ops mapping and contract/credits.

High level — two viable paths that keep things simple for Catalyst:

Option A — Targeted match (preferred for short timeline)
- Effective discount: 18% off list on committed monthly units (12-month minimum).
- Onboarding credit: $100k applied as account credit across first 3 billing cycles.
- Seat tiers: map their dev/prod/enterprise to our SKU tiers 1/2/3 with capped overage pricing.
- SLA: standard SLA applies; we can include a 30-day tech escalation playbook.
- Constraints: requires a 12-month committed baseline and a minimum monthly throughput.

Option B — Full economic match with operational uplift
- Effective discount: 25% to mirror incumbent but requires a 24-month committed term and a 10% volume growth clause year-over-year.
- Onboarding credit: $150k one-time credit, plus a single-week professional services (PS) sprint included.
- SLA: elevated SLA (faster incident SLA) and named technical liaison for the first 90 days.
- Constraints: needs legal sign-off on a limited-fallthrough clause and a defined migration acceptance test.

Notes: we do not typically give unconditional multi-year price parity without contract protections (usage floors, roll-off notice, or growth gates). I attached a short workbook (redwood_competitive_options.xlsx) with the math for both options and a quick pivot showing net TCO under Catalyst’s expected monthly units.

Next steps: if you prefer Option B we should schedule Marissa + legal to cover contract language. If Option A looks workable we can send a templated term sheet and a draft SOW for the onboarding credit.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Sales Director | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: redwood_competitive_options.xlsx (spreadsheet, 320KB)

From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@catalyst.ai>

Subject: Re: Pricing and packaging clarification (RFP attached)

Naomi — thanks for the clear options. A couple of follow-ups from our side before we escalate to procurement:

1) Data residency & audit logs: Option B sounds attractive, but we need confirmation that audit logs and KMS integration are available in our region within the 90-day SLA uplift period.
2) Migration egress: the incumbent is offering a direct egress credit to offset cloud transfer fees. Can Redwood make that explicit in the SOW or instead increase the onboarding credit to cover estimated egress?
3) Final question on seat-tier mapping: can you provide an ops-level table that maps their three seat types to your SKUs with expected token throughput per seat? We need that to compare monthly committed units.

If you can answer these items we can route this to procurement for a final decision by Monday.

—Rajiv
VP Engineering, Catalyst AI

Rajiv / Ellen — Jonas here, solutions engineering. Quick answers and what I'll deliver by EOD Monday: 

1) Data residency & KMS: we can confirm KMS integration and audit log export to Catalyst's S3 in us-west-2. Timeline: full integration test within 30 days (pre-go-live) and production mirror within 60 days. That fits under Option B's 90-day liaison window.

2) Migration egress: we can either label $150k of the onboarding credit as an explicit egress reimbursement in the SOW or offer a separate egress credit line item. My recommendation: keep it explicit (SOW line: "Egress reimbursement up to $150,000 against documented transfer invoices") so procurement has a clean budget line.

3) Seat-tier mapping: attached is a short ops table (included below) that maps Catalyst seat types to Redwood SKUs and expected token throughput per seat:

- Dev -> SKU-T1: 50k tokens/month per seat (non-prod profile)
- Prod -> SKU-T2: 400k tokens/month per seat (standard production)
- Enterprise -> SKU-T3: 1.2M tokens/month per seat (high-rate, low-latency)

I'll also provide a sample term sheet with the SOW language for egress reimbursement and the elevated SLA clause so Marissa and legal can review. Marissa — can you own contract language for the Option B fallthrough and the growth gate? I attached SLA-exception-notes.docx to capture proposed wording.

Thanks — Jonas
